premises: Ultrafast heating (>5000 K) and ultrarapid cooling (10^5–10^6 K/s) can be achieved via a thermal plasma jet.
Such thermal history forces co-nucleation and simultaneous condensation of multiple metal vapors.
Co-nucleation overcomes differences in elemental nucleation temperatures to yield homogeneous HEA nanoparticles.
Slower cooling allows metals with higher nucleation temperatures to lag, causing compositional inhomogeneity.
Plasma gas composition (e.g., hydrogen-rich vs. helium-rich) modulates cooling rate and thus homogeneity.
